title: Reserved namespaces
description: Validates /reserved-namespaces.json (repo root), the data file ADR-0119 Section 1 specifies: "registry/reserved-namespaces.json, one entry per namespace with the reason it is reserved." This schema file lives under tests/contracts/ rather than contracts/ because this task's declared file scope names contracts/entry.schema.json, contracts/page.schema.json and contracts/manifest.schema.json explicitly and does not add a fourth contracts/*.schema.json file; tests/contracts/** is the declared scope this validator fits inside instead (see docs/tasks/006-contracts.md Questions). Each namespace's `owner` sub-shape intentionally duplicates entry.schema.json's `owner` definition (same three fields, same numeric-id rule) rather than referencing it via $ref, because the stdlib-only validator this repository's tests use (schema_check.py) does not implement $ref resolution -- ADR-0103: duplicating five lines is the boring choice next to building a $ref resolver for one use.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this file's shape, matching the convention set by contracts/validation-report.schema.json.

namespaces.description: Namespace name -> { owner, reason }. ADR-0119 Section 1: "Phase 1 contains exactly mc and test." Represented as an object keyed by namespace, not an array, for O(1) lookup by registry CI on every PR (ADR-0119 Section 3: CI must check whether a PR touches a reserved namespace on every PR, not just occasionally).

owner.description: ADR-0119 Section 2: "bound to the organisation's numeric account id ... following ADR-0058 Section 2 unchanged -- the binding mechanism is identical to every other namespace." Same shape as entry.schema.json's `owner`.

id.description: Numeric account id, never a username string -- same rule as entry.schema.json's owner.id (ADR-0058 Section 2).

reason.description: ADR-0119 Section 1: "one entry per namespace with the reason it is reserved."
